analysis.title: Americas Business & Information Services: What's Powering Your Services Recap - 11/20/26
key_insights: Information Services fell 7% on average this week and is down 22% YTD. Business Services fell 4% on average and is up 7% YTD. The S&P 500 fell 5% this week and is up 5% YTD.

Average NTM multiples: Information Services 12.6x EV/EBITDA and 17.1x P/E, Business Services 9.4x EV/EBITDA and 17.2x P/E, S&P 500 12.3x EV/EBITDA and 17.3x P/E. Exhibits 3 and 4 show NTM P/E and EV/EBITDA multiples trending lower for both groups.

SPGI (Buy): after a non-deal roadshow, GS says the contemplated CapIQ separation should sharpen focus on benchmark-led franchises (Ratings, Indices, Energy) and improve capital allocation. GS sees mid-to-high single-digit organic revenue growth and mid-teens EPS growth.

MH (Buy): at its first Investor Day the company set an F2028-F2030 framework of 5-8% revenue growth, 7-12% EBITDA growth and 100-200+ bps of margin expansion, against a 4.1% revenue CAGR in F2022-F2026. Higher Education share gains, the K-12 ELA adoption cycle and AI monetization are the drivers.

IRM (Buy): signed data center backlog approaches $1.8bn of annualized revenue against about $1bn of current data center revenue. ALM is guided to above 25% organic growth in 2027 assuming flat memory prices, and the US Treasury contract is expected to add about $100mn of revenue in 2027.

KFY (Buy): GS came away more positive on Talent Suite differentiation (115mn assessments, 12,000+ defined jobs) and the AMS combination. Cost synergies are expected ahead of revenue synergies, and new business signings are the best near-term indicator of revenue synergy progress.

Investor feedback this week: constructive on KFY, RHI's near-term inflection viewed more favorably than its 2028-2029 outlook, MAN the opposite setup, BCO interest on rising ATM usage and the pending NATL acquisition, CTAS a favored name, and views on ROL mixed given limited evidence of a residential recovery.

ROL says digital leads fell about 20% from midway through 2Q and stayed weak through 3Q, which it attributes to AI-driven lead pressure. Mitigation includes optimizing website visibility on LLM platforms. It reaffirmed 3-4% annual pricing and 7-8% organic growth targets.

EFX expects a larger 2027 US mortgage decline than the high-single-digit decrease previously contemplated, because the mortgage market has weakened since October. Offsets include government contract wins and a doubled AI productivity target.

MCO cites about $5tn of debt maturities over four years and AI-related infrastructure at about 50% of issuance growth YTD. It flagged a tougher 4Q comparison from elevated hyperscaler issuance and bank loan repricing in the prior year.
MSCI reports TTM net subscription sales up 26% y/y with growing enterprise-wide deals. Longer sales cycles could introduce quarterly volatility.

Macro read-across: jobless claims of 203k beat consensus higher, which GS calls incrementally negative for staffers MAN and RHI. Retail sales rose 0.2% m/m in October, in line with consensus, which GS says carries negative implications for cash management at BCO.

Global debt issuance fell 18% y/y in the week of 11/9/26 and is up 7% YTD. High yield issuance fell 48%, leveraged loan issuance fell 93% and structured finance fell 40%, while investment grade rose 23%.

CY2026 consensus EPS revisions YTD average -0.9% and the median is +0.5%. The largest upward revisions are VSTS (+77.6%), MH (+19.4%) and PBI (+18.8%), and the largest downward revisions are KLC (-95.8%), BV (-46.8%) and RHI (-22.8%).

market_movers.rationale: Investor group meeting left GS incrementally more positive on data center backlog visibility, ALM cross-selling and digital solutions growth.
New F2030 framework is driven by Higher Education share gains, the K-12 adoption cycle and AI monetization.
Talent Suite differentiation and AMS cost and revenue synergies support more durable growth and margin expansion.
Contemplated CapIQ separation sharpens focus on Ratings, Indices and Energy, with durable growth and greater capital return flexibility.

sector_views.rationale: Group is down 22% YTD with NTM EV/EBITDA of 12.6x, in line with the S&P 500. GS publishes Buy views on SPGI and MH in the group.
Group is down 4% this week and up 7% YTD at 9.4x NTM EV/EBITDA. GS publishes Buy views on IRM and KFY, while the staffing names face a loosening labor market.

earnings_insights: MAN guides 4Q organic constant currency revenue growth of about 5% (company expectation, not yet reported), with Manpower up 7%. Gross margin is stabilizing near 15.9-16.0%.
MH F2027 revenue guidance is 0.6-3.4% (2.0% midpoint) and EBITDA growth guidance is 0.8-6.1% (3.5% midpoint), per company data. The F2028-F2030 targets are 5-8% revenue CAGR and 7-12% EBITDA CAGR.
MCO reiterated its 2026 guidance and flagged a tougher 4Q comparison. First-time ratings mandates rose 40% in 3Q (reported).
CLVT reiterated 10-15% FCF growth for 2027 (company outlook) and EBITDA margins of about 45%. IP ACV returned to positive growth for the first time in more than three years.

CY2026 FactSet consensus EPS estimates, 1/1/2026 vs 11/19/2026: VSTS $0.37 to $0.65, MH $1.66 to $1.99, IRM $2.27 to $2.52, SPGI $18.82 to $17.91, RHI $1.69 to $1.31, KLC $0.63 to $0.03. These are consensus estimates, not reported results.
EFX raised expected 2026 margin expansion from 75 bps to 100 bps (company outlook). New government contract ACV rose from $100mn in July to $150mn in 3Q.
Upcoming company events: VSTS F4Q earnings 12/1, HRB investor day 12/3, MSCI 4Q earnings 1/26.

risk_factors: US mortgage market weakness since October could make EFX's 2027 mortgage-related decline larger than high-single digits, and TRU says mortgage remains pressured with higher rates also weighing on auto and consumer lending.
AI-driven digital lead pressure at ROL, with digital leads down about 20% and weakness persisting through 3Q.
Loosening labor market for staffers MAN and RHI, and decelerating retail sales for BCO's cash management.
MSCI's longer enterprise sales cycles could introduce quarterly volatility.
MCO faces a tougher 4Q comparison from elevated hyperscaler issuance and bank loan repricing in the prior year.

tension_points.bull_case: ROL reiterated 3-4% annual pricing with limited customer resistance, door-to-door sales growing double digits this year and homebuilder and commercial channels performing well.
tension_points.bear_case: Digital leads fell about 20% from midway through 2Q on AI-driven lead pressure, and investors see limited evidence of a residential recovery.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Investor views hinge on evidence of a residential recovery, which the report says is limited so far.

tension_points.bull_case: Workforce Solutions has a long runway, with TWN at 170mn active records up 10% y/y and government contract ACV rising from $100mn to $150mn.
tension_points.bear_case: The US mortgage market has weakened since October, implying a potentially larger 2027 decline than the high-single-digit decrease previously contemplated.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A 2027 mortgage market decline larger than the high-single-digit decrease previously contemplated.
